formats.key: Permit(address owner,address spender,uint256 value,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)
effects: Sets the spender's allowance over the owner's USDC to exactly `value`, replacing any earlier allowance (FiatTokenV2_2 permit -> EIP2612._permit -> _approve(owner, spender, value)).
The signature can be used until `deadline`; type(uint256).max means it never expires.
Uses up the owner's current permit nonce, so the signature works only once and cancels any other unused permit with the same nonce.
formats.shown: The intent "Authorize spending of tokens", with the spender address, the maximum amount in USDC ("Unlimited" at 2^255 or more), the expiry date and the owner.

findings.title: Permit test covers only a 250 USDC amount, never the "Unlimited" threshold or a no-expiry deadline.
findings.evidence: cases/0.json message value "250000000", deadline "1780000000"; descriptor value field threshold "0x8000…" message "Unlimited"; EIP2612._permit: `deadline == type(uint256).max || deadline >= now`.
findings.fix: Add a test case with value = type(uint256).max that should render "Unlimited", and one with deadline = type(uint256).max.

findings.title: Permit deadline type(uint256).max means no expiry but shows as a far-future date.
findings.evidence: EIP2612._permit: `require(deadline == type(uint256).max || deadline >= now, ...)`; descriptor field deadline format "date", encoding "timestamp".
findings.fix: None needed. When wallets support it, render the max value as "Never expires".
